title: CRS Defense Primer: Emerging Technologies — Phase 65 Quantum review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Quantum reporting pack. The CRS primer synthesizes the defense implications of artificial intelligence, lethal autonomous systems, hypersonic weapons, directed energy, biotechnology, and quantum technology. It emphasizes maturity, operational concepts, ethics, oversight, authorization, appropriations, and the future of warfare.
key_findings: The technologies differ materially in maturity, operational use, and governance questions.
AI and autonomy create speed and data advantages but also bias, assurance, and human-control risks.
Quantum, biotechnology, hypersonics, and directed energy create distinct sensing, materials, safety, and infrastructure dependencies.
why_it_matters: Which records separate quantum research and migration policy from standards, procurement, tested interoperability, accepted cutover, and retired cryptography? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. The primer provides a nonpartisan synthesis that helps keep technology claims bounded by maturity and oversight context.
ftfn_relevance: Supports cross-topic comparison without collapsing unlike technologies into a single readiness claim.
Adds congressional oversight and appropriations questions to the research-to-deployment stack.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
The primer is a high-level synthesis and does not replace program-specific technical evidence.
